assessments.zone: Maluku rural commune, Plateau des Batéké along RN1: Mbankana area (Kinta), Mongata, Kinzono (Mampu), Dumi
assessments.evidence: The Batéké plateau of Maluku is an operation zone of FARDC Operation Ngemba (14th Military Region) against the Mobondo militia; FARDC clashed with Mobondo at Mbankana (Aug 2025) and Mobondo killed people near Mongata (Feb 2025) and at a Maluku farm (May 2026). A DDR pilot was launched in Mbankana in Dec 2025 and by Jul-Aug 2026 the government reported pacification of Mbankana-Mongata, though residents say holdout Mobondo still occupy outlying farms; towns themselves are state-held.

assessments.zone: Remote villages of eastern/southern Maluku on the Batéké plateau: Kingawa, Batsiongo (Boko health zone)
assessments.evidence: No village-specific reports found; these villages lie in the wider Plateau des Batéké area of Maluku covered by FARDC Ngemba operations, where Mobondo bands raided farms and villages in 2025-2026 (e.g. Ibi area). Assumed state/FARDC-held with Mobondo raiding risk.

assessments.zone: Kinshasa urban neighbourhoods (health areas) of Gombe, Barumbu, Kinshasa, Lingwala, Kasa-Vubu, Kalamu I/II, Ngiri-Ngiri, Bandalungwa, Kintambo, Bumbu, Makala, Ngaba, Limete/Kingabwa, Ndjili, Kimbanseke, Masina, Kikimi
assessments.evidence: Capital city with no territorial armed-group presence. Order is kept by the PNC (Kinshasa provincial police commissariats), which runs recurrent anti-gang sweeps (Operation Ndobo, latest large wave Dec 2025 with most arrests in Masina). Kuluna gangs still assault and rob residents at night (e.g. Bandalungwa, Aug 2026) and insecurity returns between operations, but gangs do not hold or govern neighbourhoods.

assessments.zone: Military camps and garrison quarters: Camp Kokolo (Kokolo 1, Kokolo 2, Base Logistique, Bataillon PM, Haut Commandement area) and the naval base quarter (Force Navale, Kingabwa)
assessments.evidence: These health areas correspond to FARDC camps (Camp Kokolo, the army's largest Kinshasa garrison with its own hospital and school, and the naval forces quarter) populated mainly by soldiers' families, where order is kept by military authorities and military police rather than the PNC.

assessments.zone: Kinshasa city (main settlement) and all urban health-area neighbourhoods of Matete, Lemba, Kisenso, Selembao, Binza Meteo, Binza Ozone, Mont Ngafula I/II, Masina II, Kingasani, Biyela and Nsele communes
assessments.evidence: National capital with communal police commissariats and sub-commissariats in every commune; arrests, detention and dispute handling are by PNC and the courts. Kuluna gangs are widespread (notably in Kisenso, Selembao and Mont Ngafula hillside neighbourhoods) and periodically targeted by police crackdowns (e.g. 'Likofi'-style operations, 2023-2025 kuluna arrests and transfers to Kaniama-Kasese), but they do not hold neighbourhoods against a permanent police presence. Based on background knowledge; no live sources retrieved.

assessments.zone: Eastern rural Maluku (Batéké plateau and Congo river villages toward Kwamouth: Bita, Inko Mabana, Ndakopembe, Point d'Interet, Sao, Ngwo, Bangombe, Impuru, Balimo, Kitshini, Mboka Paulo, Ma Mundele, Inga, Iko, Menkao 4, Bwene Kingankati)
assessments.evidence: The Mobondo militia conflict spreading from Kwamouth (Mai-Ndombe) reached the eastern villages of Maluku commune in 2023-2024 (attacks and killings on the Batéké plateau), prompting FARDC deployments that became the main permanent security force in the area; no report known of Mobondo durably holding Kinshasa villages. Current (2026) situation could not be verified - low confidence.

assessments.zone: Peri-urban and rural settlements of Nsele (Kindobo, Kibomango, Hungu, Yemo, Kindundu, Kimia), Mont Ngafula (Mfuti Fleuve, Kingantoko, Mawonda, Mbeti), Biyela (Manzanza, Manenga, Dingi Dingi) and western Maluku (Maluku centre, Madiko, Kiyungulu, DAIPN camps, Kimpoko, Menkao)
assessments.evidence: Peri-urban localities within the city-province with police sub-commissariats and territorial administration; FARDC has significant installations nearby (Kibomango training centre, DAIPN/Nsele). No known armed group holds these localities; Mobondo incursions reported from 2023-2024 were concentrated further east on the Batéké plateau. Based on background knowledge; no live sources retrieved.

units.CD1000-kinshasa-2: This unit covers most of Kinshasa's urban health-area neighbourhoods plus six villages of rural Maluku commune on the Plateau des Batéké. The city is firmly state-held: the PNC keeps order through commissariats and recurrent anti-Kuluna sweeps (Operation Ndobo), while Kuluna street gangs remain a serious but non-territorial criminal threat. Military camps (Camp Kokolo and adjacent garrison quarters, the naval base quarter) are run by the FARDC. In Maluku the FARDC (Operation Ngemba) is the main force against the Mobondo militia; after a DDR process launched in Dec 2025 the government claims pacification by mid-2026, but holdout Mobondo bands still attacked farms in May 2026, so these villages are FARDC-dominant with Mobondo raiding.
units.CD1000-kinshasa-1: Unit covers the eastern and southern communes of Kinshasa (Matete, Lemba, Kisenso, Selembao, Binza Meteo/Ozone, Mont Ngafula, Masina II, Kingasani, Biyela, Nsele) and the rural commune of Maluku. The capital is firmly state-held: day-to-day order in the urban neighbourhoods is kept by the Police Nationale Congolaise (district commissariats, PIR/LENI units), with FARDC and Republican Guard garrisons in the city; kuluna youth gangs commit frequent robberies and assaults, especially in peripheral hillside neighbourhoods (Kisenso, Selembao, Mont Ngafula), but do not displace police authority and are targeted by recurrent police operations. Peri-urban localities of Nsele, Mont Ngafula, Biyela and western Maluku (Maluku centre, Kinkole-Kimpoko axis, DAIPN camps, Kibomango) are state/PNC areas with notable FARDC presence (Kibomango training centre, DAIPN). The eastern Batéké plateau part of Maluku bordering Kwamouth (Mai-Ndombe) has seen Mobondo militia incursions since 2023-2024, answered by FARDC deployments; it is assessed as an FARDC-held operation zone with Mobondo raiding, at low confidence.
